primary.scope: Exploratory nominal95% interval conditional on the fixed out-of-fold predictions, folds and fitted models. It omits variability from refitting shared training sets and prior analytic selection; not a formal generalization or efficacy guarantee.

analysis.fit_count_note: 30 predictor specifications; actual ridge solves and width-projection least-squares operations counted separately. No iterative optimizer or RL updates.
limitations: Model definitions fixed before these diagnostic fits, after examining these development data in prior analyses. Cross-validation here is exploratory internal validation, not untouched confirmation.

Exploratory nominal95% interval conditional on the fixed out-of-fold predictions, folds and fitted models. It omits variability from refitting shared training sets and prior analytic selection; not a formal generalization or efficacy guarantee.

Residual width tests additional linear predictive value beyond the training linear span of Q1 and distance; nonlinear redundancy can still help, so this is not information-complete independence or causality.
A single fixed within-state permutation is a negative-control realization, not a permutation test or p-value.
Near-threshold active residuals are standardized to unit variance; numerical activity alone does not imply scientific importance.
All outcomes concern candidate-bank discrepancy prediction and ranking, not a new action-selection rule or policy-learning benefit.
Cross-batch transfer reuses these development batches and the same trained checkpoint; it is not confirmation or training-seed replication.

The deterministic simulator/policy means conditional rollout sampling noise is absent. Values are numerical simulator continuations, not certified exact real arithmetic. The critic's smoothed lagged-policy TD target can differ from current-actor V; this discrepancy is not uniquely optimization error. U is a twin-min one-step TD-residual proxy, not a calibrated Q1-error guarantee.
